acceptance_met: Tool choice recorded and reviewed: iai-callgrind 0.14.2 (callgrind-class, manifest-declared dev-dependency of the workspace-excluded bench crate) driving valgrind/callgrind over 8 tracked library benches with setup-excluded fixtures; wall-clock numbers from shared runners are never compared (Ir only).

Stored ratcheted baseline benchmarks/codec/perf-baseline.json keyed by arch+rustc with toolchain, valgrind and git-sha provenance; +1% tolerance; unknown keys pass with a BASELINE_MISSING notice (not a measured regression); raises restricted to baseline-change cards.

CI job perf-gate (stable, ubuntu-latest): installs valgrind + pinned iai-callgrind-runner 0.14.2 (--locked), runs on PRs touching src/protocol/, src/producer.rs, src/consumer.rs, src/net.rs or benchmarks/codec/ (git-diff filter, no new third-party action), always on main/dispatch.

bash scripts/ci-perf-gate.sh --record (8 benches recorded for aarch64-1.98.1)
python3 scripts/ci-perf-gate-extract.py --self-test (Left/Both/Right/malformed/empty fixtures; enforced at every gate startup)
cargo fmt --check + cargo clippy --all-targets --offline in benchmarks/codec (clean)
bash scripts/check-workflows.sh with PyYAML (4/4 workflows ok)
cargo deny check in benchmarks/codec: bans/licenses/sources ok; 2 reviewed unmaintained advisories (below)
limits: Stored baseline covers aarch64+rustc 1.98.1 only (measured here); CI x86_64 reports BASELINE_MISSING (pass-with-notice) until an x86_64 baseline-change card records it — valgrind cannot run under emulation so x86_64 numbers need native hardware.
Recorded values are single-run samples; observed run-to-run jitter is <=4 instructions on one bench (0.0004% vs the 1% bar), absorbed with 2500x margin.

Deny advisories: iai-callgrind pulls bincode 1.3.3 (RUSTSEC-2025-0141, declared complete upstream, harness config serialization) and proc-macro-error2 (RUSTSEC-2026-0173, build-time proc-macro only). Both unmaintained-not-vulnerable, dev-only, never shipped; root deny policy (ignore=[]) untouched; CI deny gate covers the shipped workspace only.
Job validation is via the main-push CI run (see ci_run_url in measurements), not a PR run: same job definition; the PR path-filter branch was validated by simulating its git-diff logic locally.
